plugins.name: code-reviewer
plugins.description: Crew code review: reads every PR the developer ships in a fresh context for correctness, security, performance, accessibility and tests, and posts a review whose findings each carry a failure scenario. Approve moves the ticket to In approval (QA if labelled skip_approval); request changes, back to In progress; a fourth round with issues left stops it in Ready for the Captain. Never pushes code. Use when asked to review a PR or its code, check a diff before QA, or re-review a PR after a fix.

plugins.name: crew
plugins.description: The crew's workflow, owned by no role: in a GitHub repository with a crew board it points every session at the crew-workflow skill (each step through its crew command, no asking from In Definition to In approval, stops at In approval, starts QA when the Captain moves a card to QA, stops at Ready for Merge); in one without, the session offers to create the board. Also creates crew boards. Use when asked to do, work or ship a ticket, pick up the next issue, or create a project board.

plugins.name: designer
plugins.description: UI and UX for the crew: writes the design spec a developer builds and tests against (flow, every screen state, layout, copy, accessibility) and reviews existing UI for usability, WCAG 2.2 AA and consistency with the project's own tokens. Use when asked to design or spec a screen or flow, review UX or UI, check accessibility or contrast, or make an interface consistent.

plugins.name: developer
plugins.description: The development loop end to end, test-first: implement a feature in red-green-refactor slices, refactor without changing behaviour, diagnose a bug to its proved root cause, fix it with the failing test first, bisect a regression to its commit, run the repo's checks, ship it as a ticket, branch and PR, and, when asked, rebase a PR to clear its conflicts. Use when asked to implement, refactor, debug, fix a failing or flaky test, find what broke, open a PR, or resolve its merge conflicts.

plugins.name: devops
plugins.description: CI/CD for the crew: sets up GitHub Actions that run a repo's own checks and triages failing runs to a cause and an owner. PR review links (previews) are paused for now. Never handles secret values. Use when asked to set up CI or CI/CD, fix a workflow, or find why CI is red.

plugins.name: notes
plugins.description: Keeps running notes on many topics organized in plain Markdown: captures as you go, regroups each topic into In progress, TODO, Done and Notes without losing a line, shows what is open, and turns TODO, in-progress and inline "text"(todo|wip|done) markers into GitHub tickets, with "text"(outcome) as acceptance criteria, assigned to you on your default board or one named per item. Use when asked to note something, organize notes, list open TODOs, or file notes as tickets.

plugins.name: plugin-developer
plugins.description: Builds an agent plugin from a requirements prompt: splits it into testable requirements, maps each to the component that covers it (hooks, MCP servers and scripts only when needed), stops for approval, then scaffolds, tests and gates the plugin until it validates, loads and passes. Use when the user asks to build, plan or check a plugin or Claude Code extension from requirements.

plugins.name: qa
plugins.description: Quality assurance for the crew: turns a ticket's acceptance criteria into a test plan before work starts, verifies a change in the QA column against every criterion with evidence, on its PR's head commit run locally, gives an accept or reject verdict and moves the ticket to Ready for Merge or back to In progress, and files reproducible bug tickets labelled "QA testing". Use when asked to test, QA or verify a change, check acceptance criteria, write test cases or a test plan, or report a bug.

plugins.name: scrum-master
plugins.description: Backlog refinement and sprint planning against GitHub Issues. Turns raw requests into ready stories with acceptance criteria and a size, splits the ones that are too big, and builds a sprint plan with one goal and a realistic capacity. Use when asked to refine or groom a backlog, write a user story, add acceptance criteria, estimate work, or plan the next sprint.

plugins.name: skill-trainer
plugins.description: Keeps a senior engineer's skills sharp next to a full-time job: daily and weekly plans across coding, system design, stack deep-dives, practices and builds, honest grading and spaced review, plus an interview track for coding and system design. Stack, coding language and cadence are changeable settings. Use when asked for a study plan, today's practice, a coding drill, interview practice or progress.
